profile.campus: Csquare Silicon Valley campus cluster (SFO1-SFO4, formerly Centersquare, formerly Evoque Data Center Solutions)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.address: 1500/1550 Space Park Drive, Santa Clara, CA
profile.reading:
This building is the westernmost of two structures that Csquare markets together as SFO4, part of its four building Silicon Valley campus cluster at 1500 and 1550 Space Park Drive in Santa Clara, California. The two SFO4 buildings sit roughly 300 feet apart and are mapped in OpenStreetMap as separate ways, consistent with Csquare's own SEC registration prospectus, which lists two distinct rentable units under the SFO4 code rather than one, SFO4_A at 21,724 rentable square feet, leased, 86.8 percent occupied as of March 31, 2026, and SFO4_B at 35,754 rentable square feet, company owned and fully occupied. Which of those two suffixes corresponds to this particular building could not be confirmed this session, so no individual floor area or occupancy figure is assigned to this record.

Csquare's own facility page states that the SFO4 code as a whole, meaning both buildings together, totals 57,450 square feet of raised floor with 43.1 megawatts of utility power capacity, 12.3 megawatts of UPS protected capacity, and 20.5 megawatts of generator capacity, along with SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS, NIST 800-53 PE High, ISO 27001, LEED Gold, and ENERGY STAR certifications and three carrier neutral service providers on site. Those power figures describe the combined SFO4 pair rather than this single building, and are recorded here as campus context rather than as this building's own capacity.

Csquare, Inc., trading on the New York Stock Exchange as CSQR, is the current name for a data center real estate company that says it began operations in January 2019 under the name BIF III US Aggregator (Delaware) LLC, later becoming Evoque Data Center Solutions under Brookfield affiliated ownership, then Centersquare, then Csquare, converting from a limited liability company to a Delaware corporation on June 15, 2026 ahead of an initial public offering that priced on July 16, 2026 at 21 dollars a share across 50 million shares for roughly 1.05 billion dollars gross. Brookfield Corporation retained approximately 69 percent of voting power afterward, making Csquare a controlled company under New York Stock Exchange rules. The same prospectus reports a company wide portfolio, as of March 31, 2026, of 64 sites across 21 metro markets in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, totaling roughly 389 megawatts of sellable power capacity and more than 1,700 customers, and it separately warns investors that power costs in its Boston and California markets run higher and more volatile than in its other markets, a caution this Santa Clara building sits squarely inside.

No tenant is named for either SFO4 unit in any source reviewed. The SFO airport code naming convention applied across this Santa Clara and Sunnyvale cluster, despite sitting roughly 40 miles south of San Francisco International Airport itself, reflects a Bay Area colocation naming habit that predates Csquare's current ownership and traces to the site's earlier CenturyLink and Savvis heritage.

reading.body:
Csquare SFO4 publishes 129.4 MW of combined utility power across 273,000 square feet of technical space in Santa Clara. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 129.4 MW of IT load would support roughly 3,235 racks, but that figure assumes all published utility power reaches IT equipment, which depends on the campus PUE, and the operator does not publish a PUE figure. The actual rack count available for AI workloads is therefore not derivable from the published data.

The certifications describe what the campus is qualified to host. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 qualify it for tenants whose auditors require attested controls over financial and operational systems. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment-card data environments. ISO 27001 and NIST 800-53 qualify it for tenants requiring internationally recognized and US federal information-security management frameworks, respectively. LEED certifies that the building meets a recognized environmental design standard.

In California, this site is one of 103 facilities this site has mapped, and only 8 facilities in the state have a published megawatt figure at all. Among those 8, SFO4 ranks eighth by published MW. The 7 facilities with published figures account for 185 MW combined in this site's dataset, meaning SFO4's 129.4 MW represents roughly 70 percent of that published total on its own, which reflects how few operators in California publish a capacity number rather than indicating SFO4's share of actual statewide capacity.
